common_name: Sir John Thouron Clivia (Historic Pale-Yellow Breeding Parent)

planting.note: Plant divisions or tissue-cultured offsets in deep shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil; 'Sir John Thouron' is a rare pale-yellow Clivia miniata selection that became the founding parent of the Longwood Gardens clivia breeding program started in 1976.

directions: Grow in deep, even shade in humus-rich, sharply drained soil, keeping the fleshy roots somewhat crowded for best flowering. 'Sir John Thouron' bears showy, pale yellow flowers in a ball-shaped umbel held above dark green leaves in late winter to spring, and its historical importance as the original breeding parent behind Longwood Gardens' celebrated clivia program has made it one of the most storied named clivia in Western cultivation. Give plants a cool, dry winter rest of six to eight weeks with minimal watering to trigger strong spring bloom, and avoid disturbing roots any more often than necessary, since recovery from division is slow.

planting.note: Plant divisions or tissue-cultured offsets in deep shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil; 'Longwood Debutante' was released in 2011 as the first named clivia from Longwood Gardens' breeding program.

directions: Site in deep, even shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil, allowing roots to become somewhat pot-bound for the most reliable bloom. 'Longwood Debutante' produces slightly fragrant, buttery yellow flowers with broad, overlapping petals held in a full, rounded umbel above dark green foliage, the culmination of decades of selective breeding at Longwood Gardens aimed at producing a superior yellow clivia after years in which yellow-flowered forms were rare and weak-growing. Provide a cool, dry winter rest of six to eight weeks before spring to set the strongest flower stalks, and divide congested clumps only when necessary, since flowering slows for a season after root disturbance.

planting.note: Plant divisions or tissue-cultured offsets in deep shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil; 'Longwood Fireworks' was released in 2012 as the second named clivia from Longwood Gardens' breeding program.

directions: Grow in deep, even shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil, keeping roots somewhat crowded to encourage flowering. 'Longwood Fireworks' bears large, pale yellow flowers with reflexed, backward-curving petals and prominently protruding stamens, held in a full, round umbel that gives the cultivar its explosive, firework-like appearance, a standout among Longwood Gardens' yellow breeding lines. Give a cool, dry winter rest of six to eight weeks to trigger strong spring bloom, resuming regular watering once a flower stalk emerges from the leaf axils, and divide congested clumps only when truly necessary.

common_name: Longwood Sunrise Clivia (First Orange Longwood Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant divisions or tissue-cultured offsets in deep shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil; 'Longwood Sunrise' debuted in 2014 as the third named release and the first orange-flowered selection from Longwood Gardens' breeding program.

directions: Site in deep, even shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil, allowing the fleshy roots to become somewhat pot-bound for best flowering. 'Longwood Sunrise' produces radiant orange, keeled petals with a warm yellow center, forming a round, slightly fragrant umbel above dark green foliage, after two prior yellow releases this was Longwood Gardens' first orange introduction. Provide a cool, dry winter rest of six to eight weeks before spring to encourage the strongest bloom, and divide congested clumps sparingly.

planting.note: Plant divisions or tissue-cultured offsets in deep shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil; 'Longwood Chimes' was introduced in 2016 as the fourth named release from Longwood Gardens' clivia breeding program, which began in 1976.

directions: Grow in deep, even shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil, keeping roots somewhat crowded for reliable bloom. 'Longwood Chimes' offers an unusual color break for the genus, a complex blend of bronze and burnt orange with dark red overtones around a green throat, deepening to dark red as the flowers age, a departure from the more familiar pure orange and yellow clivia strains. Give a cool, dry winter rest of six to eight weeks to set strong flower stalks, resuming regular watering once bloom spikes appear in the leaf axils, and avoid dividing clumps more often than necessary.

planting.note: Plant divisions or tissue-cultured offsets in deep shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil; 'Longwood Sunset' was released in 2017 from Longwood Gardens' clivia breeding program.

directions: Site in deep, even shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil, allowing roots to become somewhat pot-bound for the best flowering. 'Longwood Sunset' bears large flowers in soft salmon tones with a contrasting butter-yellow-and-white throat and a thin, red-orange picotee edge outlining each petal, a distinctive bicolor combination among named clivia hybrids. Provide a cool, dry winter rest of six to eight weeks before spring to encourage the strongest bloom display, and divide congested clumps only when truly necessary, since flowering slows for a season after disturbance.

common_name: Longwood Winter Green Clivia (First Green-Flowered Longwood Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant divisions or tissue-cultured offsets in deep shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil; 'Longwood Winter Green' was named by public vote in 2019 as a named release from Longwood Gardens' clivia breeding program and its first green-flowered selection.

directions: Grow in deep, even shade in humus-rich, well-drained soil, keeping the fleshy roots somewhat crowded for reliable flowering. 'Longwood Winter Green' is a rare color break for the genus, bearing creamy green petals that gently cup a throat of deeper green rather than the familiar orange, yellow, or bronze tones of most clivia. Give a cool, dry winter rest of six to eight weeks to set strong bloom stalks, and divide congested clumps only when necessary.
